header.name: Numerical Methods
header.description: This is a first course on Numerical Methods to be offered to 2nd / 3rd year undergraduate students. It covers basic topics in root finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and then moves to methods to numerically solve linear systems of equations as well as ordinary and partial differential equations. The theory involved in deriving methods as well as their error and stability properties is given due attention alongside an insistence on applying the methods, writing computer programs, obtaining numerical solutions and comparing them with analytical solutions whenever possible.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students can find roots of equations of the form f(x) = 0, interpolate functions and numerically differentiate and integrate functions with a clear understanding of convergence and accuracy.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to solve systems of linear equations using direct as well as iterative methods.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to write computer programs to solve ordinary differential equations numerically and interpret / visualize results.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to derive / analyze finite difference methods for solving partial differential equations with a clear understanding of their properties vis a vis their accuracy and stability.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to solve physical problems that can be modeled using partial differential equations numerically : generate mathematical model, specify initial and boundary conditions, apply an appropriate

lecture_topics: Preliminaries (floating point, round-off, error propagation, stability of algorithms)
Solutions of equations by iteration: Fixed point iteration, Newton's method, Secant method
Interpolation
Interpolation (contd.)
Splines
Numerical integration and differentiation
Linear systems: Gauss elimination, LU-factorization, matrix inversion, solution by iteration
Linear systems (contd.): Ill conditioning, Norms
Least squares method
Linear systems (contd.): Matrix eigenvalue problems, Approximations and error bounds for eigenvalues, power method for eigenvalues
Linear systems (contd.): Tridiagonalization: Householder's method, QR- factorization
Methods for first order ODEs: Euler method, Improved Euler (Heun) method, Runge Kutta methods
Multistep methods: Adams-Bashforth, Adams-Moulton
Methods for higher order and systems of ODEs: Euler method, Runge-Kutta methods, Runge-Kutta-Nystrom methods, Stiff systems
Introduction to partial differential equations
first order PDEs
mathematical classification of second order PDEs
characteristics
Finite difference representation of PDEs: Truncation, round off & discretization errors, Consistency, Stability, Convergence
Obtaining finite difference equations using Taylor series
Fourier or von Neumann stability analysis of finite difference schemes
Applications to model problems: Hyperbolic: Advection equation: Euler explicit, first order upwinding
Wave equation
Applications to model problems (contd.): Parabolic: Heat equation: Forward time central space method, Crank Nicolson method
Elliptic: Difference equatons for Laplace and Poisson equations
Elliptic PDEs (contd.): Dirichlet problem: Liebmann's method, ADI method
Neumann and mixed problems
Irreuglar boundary

Computational Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer (3rd Edition) by Richard H. Pletcher, John C. Tannehill and Dale A. Anderson [Chapters 2: Partial Differential Equations, 3: Basics of Discretization Methods and 4: Applications of Numerical Methods to Selected Model Equations]
Computational Fluid Dynamics : The Basics with Applications by John D. Anderson, Jr. [Chapter 4: Basic Aspects of Discretization]
